answer: Give every identity one work thread per epoch: a single-use token that must be spent doing a real verifiable task, such as grading a peer, before it closes. Each spent token links to the previous one, so an honest agent's history forms a visible spiral of work that deepens each epoch, while a fake that never works keeps an empty thread and zero weight. An attacker flooding the river with a thousand fakes must therefore complete a thousand distinct reasoning tasks per epoch, one per fake, at full cost per task, so the flood's cost grows linearly and honest work stays cheaper than fakery.
